chunks: The Prophet believes in what has been revealed to him by his Lord, and so do the faithful. Each one believes in God and His angels, His Books and the prophets, and We make no distinction between the apostles. For they say: 'We hear and obey, and we seek Your forgiveness, O Lord, for to You we shall journey in the end.'
ai.seo_question: What do the Prophet and the believers believe in according to Surah Al-Baqarah verse 285?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited alongside 2:285 as the definitive statement of creed (Aqidah), emphasizing the unity of the messengers' message and the Prophet's complete submission to divine revelation. The phrase 'We hear and we obey' (Sami'na wa ata'na) is viewed as a model of immediate, unconditional compliance with God's will, reflecting the spiritual state of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful. It underscores the theological principle that belief in all prophets is indivisible, rejecting any hierarchy that diminishes the status of earlier messengers.
